details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is renewing its efforts for a digital euro, with Executive Board member Piero Cipollone emphasizing its role in giving Europe greater control over its payment infrastructure and reducing reliance on foreign providers. A pilot program is anticipated for 2027, with a potential public launch in 2029. This initiative is presented as a means to ensure essential financial services can operate without full dependence on external companies.
title: ECB Pushes for Digital Euro Amidst Payment Sovereignty Concerns

details: As of Monday morning, October 26, 2026, Bitcoin was trading near $80,283.62, showing a 1% decrease over the past 24 hours. Ethereum also experienced a slight decline, trading around $2,325.85, down 1.3%. This follows approximately $773.5 million in net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) over two trading days on October 22 and 23, with analysts suggesting a sustained drop below the $80,000–$82,000 range could lead to further price depreciation.
title: Cryptocurrency Markets See Modest Declines as Bitcoin ETF Outflows Continue

details: Over 100 leading Israeli economists, business executives, and former public officials expressed "grave concern and anxiety" regarding Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's suggestion that Israel could use cryptocurrencies to bypass potential international banking sanctions. They warned that such a move would lead to "irreversible damage," including economic isolation, surging unemployment, and the collapse of foreign investment. The Bank of Israel also rejected the proposal, stating that cryptocurrencies cannot be used to bypass sanctions.
title: Economists Condemn Netanyahu's Proposal to Use Crypto for Sanctions Evasion

details: The Governing Council of the European Central Bank (ECB) is scheduled to hold its monetary policy meeting on October 28-29, 2026, to decide on euro area interest rates. With the current deposit rate at 2.5% and inflation at 3.8% (as of September 16), the outcome of this decision could influence market dynamics. Notably, the risk-free rate in euros now exceeds the yield offered by Ethereum staking, which could make traditional investments relatively more attractive to some investors.
title: Upcoming ECB Rate Decision: Implications for Crypto Investors

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) highlighted in its October 2026 Global Financial Stability Report that tokenized assets reached an estimated $65.1 billion in 2026. However, the report cautioned that automatic liquidation mechanisms common in tokenized lending could amplify financial stress, potentially leading to rapid and widespread sell-offs across interconnected markets. The IMF also observed that over half of tokenized US stock trading occurs outside regular market hours, with 80% of transactions involving less than one share, indicating significant retail participation and demand for fractional ownership. Concerns were also raised about the fragmentation and illiquidity of current tokenized markets.
title: IMF Warns of Liquidation Risks in Growing Tokenization Market
